title: Certify v0.10.0: The extremal graph for k(3,4) = r(I_3,L_4) = 21 is not unique — thirteen pairwise non-isomorphic, rigid, {I_3,TT_4}-free oriented graphs on 20 vertices, independently verified
description: This is an addendum (Part J) to the determination of the Erdos-Rado oriented Ramsey number k(3,4) = r(I_3,L_4) = 21 (Part G, version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21890619), answering its Question 8.1. Part G exhibits an explicit {I_3,TT_4}-free oriented graph W on 20 vertices (the lower bound for k(3,4) = 21) and asks whether W is the unique such graph up to isomorphism. The answer is NO. This release deposits thirteen {I_3,TT_4}-free oriented graphs on 20 vertices — W itself (w01_W.json, verified equal to Part G's Table 1) together with twelve more — that are pairwise non-isomorphic and every one of them RIGID (trivial automorphism group). So the 20-vertex extremal graph is not unique, and no 20-vertex extremal graph is vertex-transitive; in particular none is a Cayley digraph. THE PUBLIC UNIT IS CERTIFICATES PLUS STANDARD-LIBRARY CHECKERS: each witness ships as a JSON arc list, and three stdlib-only checkers re-derive everything from the arc lists alone. verify_witnesses.py certifies, for each of the thirteen, validity as an oriented graph, {I_3,TT_4}-freeness by EXHAUSTIVE test over all C(20,3)=1140 triples and all C(20,4)=4845 quadruples, rigidity certified two independent ways (Weisfeiler-Leman colour refinement discrete at twenty singleton colours, cross-checked by an explicit automorphism count of 1), and pairwise non-isomorphism (a canonical form read off the discrete refinement, cross-checked by an invariant fingerprint of arc count, non-adjacency-graph degree sequence, and QR_7-block count that already separates all thirteen). verify_qr7_lemma.py verifies the inputs to the QR_7 forcing lemma by exhaustive enumeration: there are exactly 240 labelled TT_4-free tournaments on 7 vertices and every one is isomorphic to the Paley tournament QR_7 = Cay(Z_7,{1,2,4}) (so it is the unique 7-vertex TT_4-free tournament; |Aut(QR_7)| = 21 and 240 = 7!/21), and there are none on 8 vertices (so every 8-vertex tournament contains a transitive TT_4). The forcing lemma follows: in any {I_3,TT_4}-free oriented graph a vertex has at most 7 non-neighbours, and a vertex with exactly 7 has its non-neighbourhood equal to QR_7 — the classical characterisation of A. Sanchez-Flores (Graphs Combin. 14 (1998), 181-200), re-established here from scratch and matching Part G, Prop. 3.3. blowup_bound.py checks that the largest {I_3,TT_4}-free tournament blow-up is QR_7[I_2] on 14 vertices (giving k(3,4) >= 15), which is six short of the extremal order 20, so the extremal family is substantially non-algebraic. All three checkers import only the Python standard library, share no code with the search that produced the witnesses, use no threads/subprocess/OS-specific calls, and return PASS on CPython 3.14.2 and 3.9.6. SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY: the result is a LOWER BOUND — at least thirteen pairwise non-isomorphic rigid extremal graphs; the exact number is not determined (the sampling that found the witnesses produced a new isomorphism class on every surviving completion, suggesting a large family, but no count is certified). Whether a QR_7 block is unavoidable — equivalently, whether the instance '{I_3,TT_4}-free on 20 vertices with every vertex having at most 6 non-neighbours' is unsatisfiable — is left OPEN. The search internals that produced the twelve additional witnesses are not part of this deposit; only the certificates and stdlib checkers are public. Computations carried out with Claude (Anthropic), directed by the author; the checkers share no code with the search. The dated novelty and verification sweep ships as SWEEP-RECORD-K34ADD-2026-08-11.md and the note as k34add-paper/note.pdf.
